summary: One release, five streams, 26 backlog items, 29 acceptance criteria. WS-A/R-0007 (anchored): fail-closed hardening of the seven engine gaps the loop hit governing its own build — serial-mode claim refusal (A1), per-task DoD LOOP_OWNED exclusion (A2), slot-env sanitization in dod_check (A3), gate/engine version-skew refusal (A4 — the blocking Design decision, resolved here), unattributed-finding warn rows in router_audit (A5), malformed-wave-entry degrade to the Task path (A6), floor clamping (A7). WS-B/R-0008: forecast recalibration against the pinned two-phase corpus (B1), engine-enforced brief-shape-before-golden-regen plan ordering (B2), symbol-less big-file ::core honesty (B3), live requirement-keyword union at component assembly (B4), graph-informed fixture-discount exception (B5). WS-C/R-0009: Windows slot activation in stage briefs (C1), components.yaml into DEFAULT_OUT_OF_SCOPE strict-or-stricter (C2), explicit --emit workflow refusal on workflow-less hosts (C3). WS-D/R-0010: five skills truthed to v2.5 (D1), facade/driver routing determinism (D2), harness rules single-sourced into references/ (D3), freshness gate extended to tp-go (D4), the 34-flag exemption list burned to empty via a generated CLI reference (D5). WS-E/R-0011: unittest-discover leg honesty via a pinned collected-count floor + no-new-pytest-only-files manifest ratchet (E1), env-mutation hygiene sweep (E2), dashboard component-node a11y + count-scaled ring radius (E3), decompose docstring truth (E4), emission-time slot-charset validation (E5), audit seam-comment truth + late-binding regression test (E6). Every change is fail-closed or fail-visible; no guardrail loosens; contract:lens-brief and contract:findings-v2 shapes are untouched.
decision: Adopt composite approach A. The A4 mechanism (the phase's one blocking open question) is decided as option (c): VALIDATOR-FINGERPRINT REFUSAL — `loop submit` stamps an engine_fingerprint (sha256 over the sorted (module, file-hash) material of the validator-surface modules loaded by the submitting process: loop, lens, lens_signals, depgraph, audit, taskplane_lite, design_contract, decompose, requirements — resolved via their __file__), and the evaluate gate compares it against the validating process's own fingerprint BEFORE running _evaluation_errors. Equal fingerprints (every non-dogfood repo, and every dogfood task not touching engine files): the comparison is the only added instruction — gate ordering and outcomes byte-unchanged. Unequal (the recorded t7 topology: worktree engine newer than the primary validator): the gate REFUSES fail-closed with a NAMED remedy — 'evidence was produced under engine <fp12> but this gate validates with <fp12>; merge the task branch into the primary (git merge tp/<task>) so one engine owns production and validation, then loop submit again' — traced as loop_gate_blocked reason=engine_skew. The loop stays at evaluate, so a re-evaluation can never be stranded: after the merge both processes run one engine, fingerprints match, and the same submission path proceeds. Option (b) (import the worktree's loop module into the gate) is DISQUALIFIED on the guardrail: it executes agent-written code in the orchestrator's validation context — a worker could author an _evaluation_errors that always passes, dissolving the L12 trust boundary that the gate validates with code the worker cannot write. Option (a) (engine-enforced merge-before-gate) merges unevaluated code into the mainline as routine, needs revert machinery the engine does not have when a post-merge evaluation fails, and cannot leave non-skew paths byte-unchanged because the ordering enforcement must run on every parallel evaluate gate. Non-blocking decisions, inside the pm's bounds — E1: pinned collected-count floor on the unittest-discover CI leg plus a named manifest of today's pytest-only files with a no-new-entries ratchet (convert-nothing: rewriting the parity/no-loosening suites to TestCase risks collection drift in exactly the suites that guard the guardrails). D5: `tp help --md` autogenerates docs/cli-reference.md from the live argparse tree (generator refuses any flag with empty help text), committed and drift-gated by the existing generated-artifacts CI pattern; the freshness test already globs docs/*.md, so _LEGACY_UNDOCUMENTED burns to empty mechanically while the new-flag ratchet gets STRICTER (every flag now needs real help prose or generation fails). B1: class-weighted forecast recalibration — functional gaps keep today's 0.5-cycle weight; NFR-coverage gaps are discounted to 0.1 ONLY when the functional axis is complete, and security/data-safety NFR gaps are NEVER discounted; the 17-task/1-fix-cycle two-phase corpus is checked in as a versioned fixture and re-scored by the test, with 2-3 synthetic under-specified requirements pinned as the no-under-warn negative corpus.

gains: Every WS-A change is a refusal or a widening — nothing merges, reorders, or executes anything new on the happy path, so 'non-skew/well-formed paths byte-unchanged' is provable by running the existing suites unchanged

A4(c) needs no code-execution change and no gate reordering: the trust boundary (gate validates with code the worker cannot author) is preserved exactly, and the refusal message mechanizes the diagnosis that took hand-debugging in Phase 2
E1 floor + manifest closes the widening without rewriting the parity/no-loosening suites (the highest-risk files to churn); the floor is a one-line honest invariant
D5 generation makes flag documentation structural: a future flag without help prose cannot ship (generator refuses), and the freshness corpus picks the reference up with zero test changes
B1 keeps both scorer axes and every warning path; only the forecast weighting learns from the corpus, and the no-under-warn corpus is pinned so flattening is mechanically impossible

The engine_fingerprint field grows the submission payload (additive; no golden covers loop submit output)
E1's floor must be maintained on suite growth (ratchet direction only: raising it is routine, lowering it is a reviewed change)

tradeoffs.revisit_when: The dogfood loop hits a skew the fingerprint cannot see (evidence authored under a third engine while submit/gate agree) — then A4 escalates to stamping the fingerprint into .eval/verdict.json itself; or the pytest-only manifest stops shrinking for two releases — then E1's convert path is re-scored; or the recalibrated forecast under-predicts a real fix cycle on a well-scoped task — then the corpus gains the miss and the weights re-fit

alternatives.name: A4 alternative (a): engine-enforced merge-before-gate ordering
alternatives.description: In parallel mode, the evaluate gate refuses to validate any task whose branch is not yet merged into the primary (or at least any task whose diff touches engine paths), forcing the merge to precede validation so the primary always validates with the merged — newest — engine.

gains: Structurally eliminates the skew for dogfood repos: after the merge there is exactly one engine
No new fingerprint machinery; the rule is a simple ordering check
costs: Merges UNEVALUATED code into the mainline as engine-enforced routine — inverts the evaluate-PASS-then-merge order that every instruction, test, and the human mental model pin; a failed post-merge evaluation needs revert machinery the engine does not have

Cannot leave non-skew paths byte-unchanged: the ordering check must run on every parallel evaluate gate, and scoping it to 'engine-touching diffs' requires a path heuristic that is repo-layout-specific (vendored engines escape it) — the exact class of guess A4 exists to remove
Reorders the most load-bearing sequence in the engine (the spec's named risk) for ALL tasks to fix a condition that occurs only when the governed repo is the engine itself
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The loop grows first-class merge/revert steps as engine-owned state transitions (flow-as-data, WS1) — then ordering enforcement becomes expressible without inventing recovery machinery

alternatives.name: A4 alternative (b): validate with the agent workspace's engine (import the worktree's modules)
alternatives.description: The gate sys.path-injects the task worktree's taskplane/ and imports its loop module, running THAT _evaluation_errors so validation semantics always match the evidence-producing engine.

gains: Validation semantics match the worktree engine by construction — the skew disappears without any refusal or extra merge step
costs: DISQUALIFYING: executes agent-written code in the orchestrator's gate context — the worktree's loop.py is the WORKER'S OWN diff, so a worker could ship an _evaluation_errors that returns [] and gate itself; the L12 trust boundary (evidence validated by code the worker cannot author) dissolves exactly at the gate it protects
sys.path/module-cache injection is fragile: loop/lens/depgraph name collisions poison the primary process for every subsequent gate in the same run
Un-testable byte-unchanged claim: which engine validated becomes data-dependent, so 'non-skew paths unchanged' cannot be pinned structurally
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Never in this architecture — it would require a sandboxed, attested validation runtime (a different trust model than the cooperative-plus-hook harness)

alternatives.name: E1 alternative: convert all ten pytest-style files to unittest.TestCase
alternatives.description: Rewrite the ten zero-TestCase files so unittest discover collects everything and the second CI leg runs the full suite.

gains: Both runners exercise the whole battery — the honest maximum
No floor to maintain; the leg's count tracks the suite automatically
costs: The ten files include the parity, no-loosening, stage-wave, and review-discipline suites — churning the exact tests that pin guardrail behavior risks silent collection drift (a mis-converted parametrization collects fewer cases and nobody notices, which is E1's own defect class reintroduced by its fix)
Large diff (thousands of lines) with zero behavior value for users; review attention is finite in a 26-item phase
pytest idioms in those files (fixtures, parametrize, tmp_path) have no 1:1 unittest form — conversion is a rewrite, not a rename
tradeoffs.revisit_when: The manifest ratchet stalls (no file converted for two releases) or a runner-specific defect escapes through a pytest-only file — then convert file-by-file, floor ratcheting up with each

alternatives.name: B1 alternative: flatten the scorer (drop or globally down-weight the NFR axis)
alternatives.description: Fix the 0.33 over-prediction by reducing the NFR axis's contribution to score and forecast across the board.

gains: Trivial change; immediately matches the two-phase corpus (which contains almost no NFR-caused fix cycles)
costs: Strictly worse than the miss it fixes (the spec's named risk): an under-specified risky requirement — no security NFR on an enforcement-touching change — would warn LESS, and the corpus cannot defend against that because 17 well-run tasks contain no counterexample
Conflates two different signals: 'NFR unstated on a well-scoped task' (cheap, rarely costs a cycle) and 'functional shape unresolved' (the thing that actually predicts cycles)
Un-revisitable: once flattened, future retros have no axis left to recalibrate
tradeoffs.revisit_when: Never as stated; the class-weighted form in A is the bounded version of this idea (discount only when functional is complete, never for security/data-safety)

alternatives.name: D5 alternative: hand-write prose docs for the 34 legacy flags
alternatives.description: Document each _LEGACY_UNDOCUMENTED flag in docs/ by hand and shrink the exemption list to empty without a generator.

gains: Prose can carry intent and examples a generated reference cannot
costs: Re-creates the drift class this phase exists to retire: hand-written flag docs fall behind the argparse tree the moment a flag changes, and only the flag's NAME is checked by the freshness test — stale help prose passes forever
34 flags of hand prose is the highest-cost, lowest-leverage work in the phase, and the ratchet still permits a future flag documented by a bare name-mention
The repo already proves the better pattern: generated lens catalog + CI drift check (ci.yml:113-118)
tradeoffs.revisit_when: A flag needs conceptual documentation beyond its help text — then a prose section supplements (never replaces) the generated reference

rollout.strategy: All five streams land fail-closed and additive within one release, sequenced by the approved priority (WS-A first, WS-B second, WS-D third, WS-C/WS-E folding into waves). WS-A: each item is an independent commit-sized change with its pinned test landing in the same diff; A4 lands submit-stamp and gate-comparison together (the field is meaningless alone); the B2 ordering rule this phase ships governs this phase's own plan (brief-shape tasks before any goldens regen task). Goldens: exactly one regeneration diff per causing task via regen.py (C1 stage prompts; any B-stream routed-set change), CI parity green after each. WS-D: skills rewrite (D1/D2) lands with the D4 minor-pin so the freshness gate goes green in the same diff; D3's references/ extraction lands with its drift check; D5's generator + committed reference + CI drift leg land together. WS-E: the floor script pins the count measured at its landing commit; the env guard lands after the sweep fixes so it is born green. Dogfood note: the moment A4 lands, this repo's own remaining waves become subject to skew refusals when tasks touch engine files — the remedy (merge first) is the documented flow and validates the mechanism on the loop that requested it.
rollout.rollback: Per item, no data migration anywhere. A1/A2/A3/A5/A6/A7/B3/B4/B5/E3/E4/E5: revert the commit — each is a localized behavior change with its tests. A4: revert removes the stamp and the comparison together; submissions carrying the extra field remain valid (unknown keys ignored by older gates). B1: revert the weight change; the corpus fixture stays (data, harmless). B2: revert removes the plan-gate rule; existing plans unaffected. C1: revert + regen.py restores prior golden bytes. C2: remove 'components.yaml' from DEFAULT_OUT_OF_SCOPE — the family returns to its prior strictly-smaller set. C3: revert restores force-print (the old, documented-acceptable behavior). D-stream: docs/skills revert freely; the references/ pointer structure degrades to today's restatements; the CI drift leg is an independent step that can be disabled without touching the suite. E1: ci.yml can call the raw discover command again; the script is additive. E6: comment text reverts with the test that pins it.
